advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the two 'legacy fcntl name' tests to patch lock_kernel.fcntl/msvcrt (or otherwise force NoExclusiveLegError) so they actually exercise the no-primitive fallback instead of patching the dead marker.fcntl name.
evidence: marker.py no longer defines fcntl: search_files for 'fcntl' in src/rebar/reducer/marker.py returns only the stale docstring line 67, no import or use
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:18-22 imports the lock primitives from rebar._store.lock_kernel, so the fcntl symbol actually used lives in lock_kernel, not marker
raising=False makes setattr create a brand-new module attribute that no code reads, so the delay/fallback path under test is never entered — the test passes via the real fcntl.flock path
advisory.finding: The two tests test_write_marker_returns_when_legacy_fcntl_name_is_none and test_remove_marker_returns_when_legacy_fcntl_name_is_none patch a nonexistent attribute (marker.fcntl) with raising=False, so the patch has no effect on execution: marker.py no longer imports or references fcntl (locking is delegated to lock_kernel, which holds the real fcntl module). These tests pass because the real POSIX lock succeeds, not because any fallback guard is exercised — their green verdict is indistinguishable from the guarded path never running, and they would still pass even if the NoExclusiveLegError fallback were broken.
scenarios: Refactor that breaks marker's NoExclusiveLegError fallback would still show these two tests green
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `monkeypatch.setattr(marker, "fcntl", None, raising=False)` with `monkeypatch.setattr(lock_kernel, "fcntl", None)` and `monkeypatch.setattr(lock_kernel, "msvcrt", None)` so the fallback path is genuinely triggered.

src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:42 (write_marker) was updated to `Acquires an exclusive lock on <ticket_dir>/.write.lock (created if absent),`

scenarios: Reader of remove_marker docstring is misled that fcntl is used directly
advisory.suggested_fix: Change line 67 to: 'Acquires an exclusive lock on <ticket_dir>/.write.lock (created if absent),'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the two legacy-fcntl-name tests to drive the real no-primitive fallback (patch `lock_kernel.fcntl`/`lock_kernel.msvcrt` to None) instead of the nonexistent `marker.fcntl` attribute.
evidence: search of src/rebar/reducer/marker.py for `fcntl` returns only line 67 (a docstring), i.e. marker no longer imports or dereferences fcntl

Inverted-trace: breaking the `except NoExclusiveLegError: yield` branch in `_marker_lock` (marker.py:29-31) would leave both tests green, since with the real fcntl present the code never reaches that branch — the tests assert only that a marker is created/removed on the normal path.
advisory.finding: The two RED-guard tests monkeypatch `marker.fcntl` with `raising=False`, but the diff removed all `fcntl` references from marker.py (only a stale docstring mention remains); marker.py never reads any `fcntl` attribute, so the patch sets an unused name and the tests merely run the normal happy path (real fcntl available). They are regression-blind: they do not exercise the new NoExclusiveLegError fallback branch and would still pass if that fallback were broken.
scenarios: Regression in the new no-primitive lock fallback (`except NoExclusiveLegError`) ships undetected because these named guard tests exercise the wrong code path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `monkeypatch.setattr(marker, "fcntl", None, raising=False)` with `monkeypatch.setattr(lock_kernel, "fcntl", None); monkeypatch.setattr(lock_kernel, "msvcrt", None)` so the tests actually hit the `NoExclusiveLegError` fallback in `_marker_lock`.
